entries.german: ergleich zwiſchen Conrad, herrn von Bickenbach, vnd Eberhard Schenk, herrn zu Erpach, über die Bertheilung ihrer beiderſeitigen Rechte an Saudie, Gütern und Gefällen zu Spachbrücken, Zyelhard und Habeſheim. Ich Conrad Rüde, Burggraue zu Wildenburg¹), Engelhard von Rosenberg vnd Heinrich Pilgerin, Ebirhard Rüde von Bodenkein vnd Synant von Rosenberg, Edelknechte, gekorn Ratlude in den Sachen zwiſchen hern Conrad, herren zü Bickenbach vnd hern Ebirhard Schen- ken, herren zü Erpach bekennen vffenlichen an dyſem briefe vnd tun kunt allen den, die in ſehent odir hörent leſen, daz wir geſchieden, geriechtet vnd gemacht han vmb die zweiunge, alz sie biz her züſchen einander gehabt hant biz uf dyſen hutigen dag: czu dem erſten male Scheiden, riechten vnd machen wir vmb die ſaudie zü Spachbrücken, zü Ziegelhard vnn zü Habeſheim uff des vorgenanten hern Ebirhart Schenken teile, daz her Ebirhart Schenke vorgenant hern Conrad von Bickenbach ein virteil geben ſal vnd ein güt gein dem andern teile an der ſaudie vnn gliche virteiln in yecelichen den vorgenanten dorfen vnd sollen darvmb Lozen, welche teil danne dem von Bickenbach vorgannt zü teile wirt, do ensal der vorgannt her Ebirhard Schencke keyne fau- die uſſe haben, noch atzunge, als ſaudie recht iſt, danne von der güden ſine zinse, gulte, welcherley die sy, Beſteheupt, hertrecht vnd libes bede. Ez ist ouch geredt, welche hoſe by hern Vlriche selgen von Bi- ckinbach fri sint geweſt, die sollen ouch furbaz fri sin vnd by der frihede vnn rechten bliben, als sie biz her kome sint vnd kuntlichen die friheid vorbrengen. Werez aber, daz sie biz her fauſthaft wern ge-weſt, so sollen sie ouch furbaz fauſthaft sin mit dinſten vnn aczungen, noch ſaudie recht. Ouch enſol der vorgannt von Bickenbach kein ſaudie haben vff den andern drin teiln des Schenken güden, die von vme geteilt sin. Werz ouch daz der vorgannt von Bickenbach Lude hette odir gewunne in den vorgannten dorfen, In des vorgannten hern Ebirhart Schenken drin teiln, do ſol ouch der von Bickenbach vorgannt sine Beſteheupt vnd Libesbede uſſe haben ane hindernisse des vorgannten Schenken vnn der sinen. Ez ist ouch geredt, soliche gulte, als dem vorgannten von Bicken- bach Jerlichen fallende sint, die yme der Schenke vorgannt Jerlichen reichet, dez sal er yme reichen vnd geben nach dem rechten, als die alten briefe beſagent, die sie bederſyten dar vber haben vnn in alten vnder einander geben hant. Vnd des zu vrkunde so han ich Conrad Rüde, Burggraue zu Wil- denburg, Engelhard von Rosenberg vnn Heinrich Pilgerin, Ritter vor- gannt vnd Ebirhard Rüde von Bodenkein, Synant von Rosenberg, Edel- knechte ouch vorgannt, vnſer Inſiegel zü festen gezügnisse vnn guder feſter ſicherheid an dyſen brief gehangen. Vnn ich Conrad herre zü Bickenbach vnn Ebirhard Schenke, herre zü Erpach vorgannt Bekennen offenlich an dyſem briefe, daz alle dyese vorgannten schei- dungen vnn Richtungen mit vnſerm wizzn vnn guden willen ist ge- ſchehen vnn globen daz ouch mit guden truwen an eydes stat vor vns vnn fur alle vnſer erben stede vnn feste zü halten ane alle geuerde. Vnd han des zü vrkunde vnſere Inſiegel ouch zü der vorgannten funfe Inſiegele an dyſen brief gehangen, der geben iſt vf den neſten Montag noch Sant Peters tage in der erne, den man nennet zu Latine Vincula Petri, Nach gots geburte drüczehen hundert vnd sehzcig Jare. Von allen Siegeln iſt nur daz dez Synant von Roſenbach noch vorhanden. Fehlerhaft abgedruckt bei Schneider C. H., u. N. XXXVII 2.
entries.english: Agreement between Conrad, Lord of Bickenbach, and Eberhard Schenk, Lord of Erpach, concerning the division of their respective rights to dower, goods, and revenues in Spachbrücken, Ziegelhard, and Habesheim. I, Conrad Rüde, Burggrave of Wildenburg¹), Engelhard von Rosenberg and Heinrich Pilgerin, Ebirhard Rüde von Bodenkein and Synant von Rosenberg, noble knights, chosen arbiters in the matters between Lord Conrad, Lord of Bickenbach and Lord Ebirhard Schenk, Lord of Erpach, openly acknowledge by this letter and make known to all who see or hear it, that we have decided, judged, and made an agreement concerning the disputes that they have had with each other until this day: Firstly, we decide, judge, and make an agreement concerning the dower in Spachbrücken, in Ziegelhard, and in Habesheim, on the part of the aforementioned Lord Ebirhard Schenk, that the aforementioned Ebirhard Schenk shall give one part to the aforementioned Conrad von Bickenbach and an equal part to the other part of the dower, and equal parts in each of the aforementioned villages, and they shall therefore draw lots for these parts, and whichever part falls to the aforementioned Bickenbach, the aforementioned Lord Ebirhard Schenk shall have no dower from it, nor claims, as is the right of dower, except for the good rents and duties of whatever kind they are, including principal, customary rights, and lifelong rights. It is also agreed that those houses which belonged to the late Lord Ulrich von Bickenbach were free shall also remain free in the future and remain in their freedom and rights, as they have been until now and openly demonstrate their freedom. But if they were subject to dower until now, they shall also be subject to dower in the future, with services and claims, but not dower rights. English Translation of image\_e61638.jpg: Also, the aforementioned from Bickenbach shall have no dower from the other three parts of the Schenk's goods that are divided by him. Should the aforementioned Bickenbach acquire people or gain in the aforementioned villages, in the three parts of the aforementioned Lord Ebirhart Schenk, then the aforementioned Bickenbach shall also have his principal and lifelong rights from them, without hindrance from the aforementioned Schenk and his. It is also agreed that such payments, as are annually due to the aforementioned Bickenbach, which the Schenk annually pays him, he shall pay him and give him according to the right, as the old letters attest, which they have on both sides and have given to each other in old times. And for this, I, Conrad Rüde, Burggrave of Wildenburg, Engelhard von Rosenberg, and Heinrich Pilgerin, knight aforesaid, and Ebirhard Rüde von Bodenkein, Synant von Rosenberg, noble knights also aforesaid, have affixed our seals to this letter for firm testimony and good, firm security. And I, Conrad, Lord of Bickenbach, and Ebirhard Schenk, Lord of Erpach, aforesaid, openly acknowledge by this letter that all these aforesaid divisions and directions have occurred with our knowledge and good will, and we promise that we will steadily and firmly uphold them with good faith, by oath, for us and for all our heirs, without any fraud. And for this, we have also affixed our seals, and the aforesaid five seals, to this letter, which is given on the next Monday after Saint Peter's Day in the spring, which is called in Latin Vincula Petri, after God's birth, thirteen hundred and sixty years. Of all seals, only that of Synant von Rosenberg is still present. Incorrectly printed by Schneider C. H., u. N. XXXVII 2.
